classificationReport.criteria: C4 (project CLAUDE.md): High = direct asset loss / valid attack path no hypotheticals; Medium = protocol function/availability or value leak with stated assumptions + external requirements; QA/Low = state handling, spec deviations, centralization, defensive gaps.

classifiedFindings.lawNote: Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun (in scope as operational hazard). Releasers/owner trusted; no malicious-owner framing.

classification.assetImpact: None. USDC custody can still move during a pause, but release() can only send to the owner-pinned `batchMinter` (the intended sink); rescueERC20() is onlyOwner. No third party gains funds; total backing is conserved (relocated, not destroyed).
attackPath: Requires either a trusted whitelisted releaser calling release() or the owner calling rescueERC20() while the dispatcher is paused.
Consequence is surprising-pause-semantics, not asset loss: pausing dispatch() halts mint/debt accrual but does not freeze custody.
classification.likelihood: n/a for exploitation; the hazard is a configuration surprise that materializes only if the owner pauses expecting a full custody freeze without also revoking releasers.
classification.assumptions: Owner and releasers are non-malicious (KI-4/KI-5). batchMinter is the intended USDC sink.
classification.externalRequirements: None that enable theft; the only requirement is that the owner paused expecting custody to be frozen.

classifiedFindings.escalationCheck: Cannot reach Medium: no value leak (USDC reaches the intended sink, fully conserved), no protocol-function/availability degradation (the mint/debt side IS paused), and no in-scope value-leak path without invoking owner malice. KI-4/KI-5 grant trust for the pause ACTION but not for the non-obvious SEMANTIC gap, so it is correctly retained rather than suppressed — landing at Low as an operational footgun with safe-config guidance.
classifiedFindings.safeConfigGuidance: To truly freeze custody during a pause, the owner must also revoke all releasers (setReleaser(x, false)); pausing dispatch() alone only freezes inbound mint/debt accrual. Document pause semantics accordingly.
classifiedFindings.justification: Surprising pause semantics on the story-043 dispatcher: pausing halts mint/debt but not custody; a trusted releaser can still move held USDC to the intended owner-pinned sink. No theft, no unbacked phUSD, no availability loss => Low operational footgun, not Medium.

classifiedFindings.plausibility: n/a (latent defensive gap, no live path)
classifiedFindings.lawNote: Law-3 borderline footgun surfaced honestly at QA. Not a malicious-owner vector; latent only under a future non-default setMinter() repoint.

classification.assetImpact: None in shipped wiring. dispatch is onlyMinter and NFTMinterV2 dispatches exactly its measured balance-delta `actualReceived`, so accrued mint-debt == on-contract USDC by construction; the dropped require(bal>=amount) is trivially satisfied and never trips.
attackPath: No live attack path. _dispatch here omits the sibling NudgeRatchet's in-contract require(bal >= amount) backing tripwire (defense-in-depth relocated off-contract to the minter's measured-delta discipline).

Latent ONLY under speculative future code: a non-default setMinter() repoint to a caller that passes an un-measured `amount` not backed by an actual transferFrom, which would then accrue debt without on-contract USDC.
That precondition does not exist at f46a5cb.
classification.likelihood: very low / latent — requires future non-default rewiring that does not yet exist; speculation on future code per C4 'Speculation on future code without demonstrated root cause'.
classification.assumptions: Shipped wiring (NFTMinterV2 measured-delta dispatch) remains in place.
classification.externalRequirements: A future setMinter() repoint to a non-measured-amount minter — not present in scope.

classifiedFindings.escalationCheck: Cannot reach Medium: no demonstrated live root cause and no in-scope value-leak path; the only impact path is gated behind speculative future rewiring. C4 explicitly discounts speculation on future code without a demonstrated root cause. Correctly a defense-in-depth / robustness QA item. Kept SEPARATE from suppressed DEDUP-001 (external phUSD backing model) per econ-scanner instruction — this is the narrower dropped in-contract assertion.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Restore parity with the sibling: read IERC20(_token).balanceOf(address(this)) in _dispatch and require(bal >= amount) (stays view; trivially satisfied in the honest held-balance path) to keep the backing invariant self-defended in-contract.
classifiedFindings.justification: Dropped in-contract defensive assertion (require(bal>=amount)) vs the sibling NudgeRatchet; no live exploit (shipped onlyMinter measured-delta dispatch makes it always satisfied), latent only under future non-default repoint => QA defensive-assertion/robustness gap, not Medium.

outputSummary.L-12 (CODE-15-001): CONFIRMED Low — operational footgun (pause does not freeze custody); funds conserved to intended sink, no value-leak/availability path.
outputSummary.Q-11 (ECON-001): CONFIRMED QA — dropped in-contract defensive assertion, latent only under speculative future setMinter repoint; no live root cause.
